        )
    )


def _fp8_lut(group_code, max_code, flush_tiny):
    """8-entry ``|E2M1| * 2**(5-delta)`` -> FP8-FNUZ byte table, as (lo, hi) dwords.

    ``group_code`` is the 32-K group's E8M0 byte, ``max_code`` the channel max.
    Includes RNE subnormals for delta in 12..18; delta >= 19 rounds to zero.
    """
    difference = max_code - group_code
    delta = fx.min(difference, 11).to(fx.Uint32) * fx.Uint32(0x08080808)
    lo = (fx.Uint32(0x6C686080) - delta) & fx.Uint32(0xFFFFFF00)
    hi = fx.Uint32(0x7C787470) - delta
    if const_expr(flush_tiny):
        # Approximation: drop groups < 2**-11 of this channel's largest scale.
        return (
            (difference > 11).select(fx.Uint32(0), lo),
            (difference > 11).select(fx.Uint32(0), hi),
        )
    for diff, low, high in (
        (12, 0x0C080400, 0x1C181410),
        (13, 0x06040200, 0x14100C08),
        (14, 0x03020100, 0x0C080604),
        (15, 0x02010000, 0x06040302),
        (16, 0x01000000, 0x03020201),
        (17, 0, 0x02010100),
        (18, 0, 0x01000000),
    ):
        lo = (difference == diff).select(fx.Uint32(low), lo)
        hi = (difference == diff).select(fx.Uint32(high), hi)
    lo = (difference >= 19).select(fx.Uint32(0), lo)
    hi = (difference >= 19).select(fx.Uint32(0), hi)
    return lo, hi


def _fp4x8_to_fp8x8(raw, lut):
    """Eight consecutive FP4 nibbles (one i32) -> v8 FP8-FNUZ MFMA operand."""
    raw = fx.Uint32(raw)
    low, high = lut
    even = _perm_u32(high, low, raw & 0x07070707)  # nibbles 0,2,4,6
    odd = _perm_u32(high, low, (raw >> 4) & 0x07070707)  # nibbles 1,3,5,7
    parts = []
    for mag, sign in (
        (even, (raw & 0x08080808) << 4),
        (odd, raw & fx.Uint32(0x80808080)),
    ):
        # FNUZ has no -0 (0x80 is NaN): clear the sign of zero-magnitude bytes.
        zeros = (~(mag + fx.Uint32(0x7F7F7F7F))) & fx.Uint32(0x80808080)
        parts.append((mag | sign) & ~zeros)
    lo = _perm_u32(parts[1], parts[0], 0x05010400).bitcast(fx.Int32)
    hi = _perm_u32(parts[1], parts[0], 0x07030602).bitcast(fx.Int32)
    return fx.Vector.from_elements([lo, hi], fx.Int32).bitcast(fx.Float8E4M3FNUZ)


def _channel_factor(exponent):
    """2**(exponent-127-5) as f32 (subnormal-safe)."""
    normal = ((exponent - 5).to(fx.Uint32) << 23).bitcast(fx.Float32)
    subnormal = (fx.Uint32(1) << (exponent + 17).to(fx.Uint32)).bitcast(fx.Float32)
    return (exponent >= 6).select(normal, subnormal)


def _fp8_frag8(v8):
    t = fx.make_rmem_tensor(fx.make_layout(8, 1), fx.Float8E4M3FNUZ)
    t.store(v8)
    return t


def _mma_fp8(mma_atom, acc, a8, b8):
    """acc += A(16x32) * B(32x16), one MFMA(16,16,32,fp8 FNUZ)."""
    fx.gemm(mma_atom, acc, _fp8_frag8(a8), _fp8_frag8(b8), acc)

@functools.cache
def compile_a8w4_gemm1(
    *,
    D_HIDDEN,
    D_INTER,
    NE,
    BM=64,
    TILE_N=128,
    TILE_K=256,
    b_cache_mod=1,
    xcd_swizzle=0,
    waves_per_eu=None,
    flush_tiny=True,
):
    """Build the A8W4 stage1 launcher.

    Launch args (raw device pointers): ``x`` fp8 [tokens, K], ``x_scale`` f32
    [tokens], ``w`` mxfp4 [E, 2*inter, K/2] (standard preshuffle), ``w_scale`` e8m0
    (shuffled), ``w_exp`` int32 [E, 2*inter] (``channel_exponents``),
    ``sorted_expert_ids``, ``num_valid_ids``, ``sorted_ids``, ``out`` bf16
    [sorted_size, inter], then ``tokens``, ``grid`` and the stream.
    """
    K = D_HIDDEN
    INTER = D_INTER
    N_OUT = 2 * INTER  # gate | up
    NUM_WAVES = 4
    assert K % TILE_K == 0 and TILE_K % 128 == 0, f"bad K={K} / TILE_K={TILE_K}"
    assert N_OUT % 256 == 0, f"2*inter_dim must be a multiple of 256, got {N_OUT}"
    assert INTER % TILE_N == 0, f"inter_dim must be a multiple of TILE_N={TILE_N}"
    assert TILE_N % (NUM_WAVES * 16) == 0, f"TILE_N must be a multiple of 64"
    assert BM % 16 == 0, f"BM must be a multiple of 16, got {BM}"
    assert (BM * TILE_K) % (256 * 16) == 0, "A tile must be whole 16 B per thread"

    NUM_N_BLOCKS = INTER // TILE_N
    K_TILES = K // TILE_K
    M_REPEAT = BM // 16  # 16-row MFMA blocks per tile
    N_REPEAT = TILE_N // NUM_WAVES // 16  # 16-col MFMA blocks per wave (gate and up)
    K_STEPS = TILE_K // 32  # MFMA K32 steps per tile
    K_GROUPS = TILE_K // 128  # 128-K groups: one W dwordx4 + one scale dword each
    A_LOADS = BM * TILE_K // (256 * 16)  # 16 B A copies per thread per tile
    LDS_BYTES = BM * TILE_K  # fp8 A tile, single slot

    # W (mxfp4) N-major preshuffle in bytes: (N/16, K/128, klane=4, nlane=16, kpack=16).
    W_K0 = K // 128
    W_BYTES = NE * N_OUT * K // 2
    # E8M0 scale preshuffle (dwords): (N/32, Kpad/256, klane=4, nlane=16); each dword
    # packs [kpack=2] x [npack=2] bytes.
    SCALE_K_PAD = ((K + 255) // 256) * 256
    SC_STRIDE_N0 = (SCALE_K_PAD // 256) * 64
    WS_BYTES = NE * N_OUT * (SCALE_K_PAD // 32)

    ftz_tag = "_ftz" if flush_tiny else ""
    wpe_tag = f"_w{waves_per_eu}" if waves_per_eu else ""
    kname = (
        f"a8w4_gemm1_h{K}_i{INTER}_ne{NE}_bm{BM}_tn{TILE_N}_tk{TILE_K}"
        f"_bcm{b_cache_mod}_xcd{xcd_swizzle}{wpe_tag}{ftz_tag}"
    )

    def _body(
        lds_ptr,
        arg_x,
        arg_x_scale,
        arg_w,
        arg_w_scale,
        arg_w_exp,
        arg_eids,
        arg_cumsum,
        arg_mind,
        arg_out,
        i32_ntok,
        tile,
        lane,
        wave,
    ):
        lane_div_16 = lane // fx.Int32(16)
        lane_mod_16 = lane % fx.Int32(16)

        # ---- tile decode: m-block (one expert) x n-block (inter tile) ----------
        n_block = tile % fx.Int32(NUM_N_BLOCKS)
        m_block = tile // fx.Int32(NUM_N_BLOCKS)
        e = rocdl.readfirstlane(T.i32, _raw(_global_i32_at(arg_eids, m_block)))
        bx_m = m_block * fx.Int32(BM)  # first sorted row of this m-block
        by_n = n_block * fx.Int32(TILE_N)
        inter_i32 = fx.Int32(INTER)

        # ---- W operand resources ------------------------------------------------
        expert_off = e * fx.Int32(N_OUT)
        layout_w = fx.make_layout(
            (N_OUT // 16, W_K0, 4, 16, 16), (W_K0 * 1024, 1024, 256, 16, 1)
        )
        w_tiles = _global_i32_buffer_tiles(arg_w, min(W_BYTES, 0xFFFFFFFF), 4)
        w_atom = fx.make_copy_atom(fx.rocdl.BufferCopy128b(b_cache_mod), fx.Int32)
        ws_tiles = _global_i32_buffer_tiles(arg_w_scale, min(WS_BYTES, 0xFFFFFFFF), 1)
        ws_atom = fx.make_copy_atom(fx.rocdl.BufferCopy32b(0), fx.Int32)

        # ---- output resource: [cumsum0, INTER] bf16, OOB stores are dropped -----
        cumsum0 = _global_i32_at(arg_cumsum, fx.Int32(0))
        out_rsrc = buffer_ops.create_buffer_resource_from_addr(
            _raw(fx.Int64(arg_out)),
            num_records_bytes=_raw(fx.Int64(cumsum0) * fx.Int64(INTER * 2)),
        )

        # ---- A operand: gather BM sorted rows of x -> LDS (via VGPRs on gfx942) -
        # Extent = the real [tokens, K] alloc so padding rows (token >= tokens) read 0.
        x_tiles = fx.logical_divide(
            _global_i32_buffer_view(
                arg_x, fx.Int64(i32_ntok) * fx.Int64(K // 4) * fx.Int64(4)
            ),
            fx.make_layout(4, 1),
        )
        x_atom = fx.make_copy_atom(fx.rocdl.BufferCopy128b(2), fx.Int32)
        lds_flat = fx.make_view(
            fx.recast_iter(fx.Int32, lds_ptr), fx.make_layout(LDS_BYTES // 4, 1)
        )
        lds_tiles16 = fx.logical_divide(lds_flat, fx.make_layout(4, 1))
        lds_tiles8 = fx.logical_divide(lds_flat, fx.make_layout(2, 1))
        lds_write_atom = fx.make_copy_atom(fx.UniversalCopy128b(), fx.Int32)
        lds_read_atom = fx.make_copy_atom(fx.UniversalCopy64b(), fx.Int32)

        def _swizzle(row, col_bytes):
            # A-LDS bank-conflict XOR swizzle; applied to the GMEM source column on
            # the write (LDS destination linear) and to the LDS column on the read.
            return col_bytes ^ ((row & fx.Int32(TILE_K // 16 - 1)) * fx.Int32(16))

        tx = fx.Int32(gpu.thread_id("x"))
        a_rows, a_cols_dw, a_row_base_dw = [], [], []
        for i in range_constexpr(A_LOADS):
            idx_dw = tx * fx.Int32(4) + fx.Int32(i * 256 * 4)
            row = idx_dw // fx.Int32(TILE_K // 4)
            a_rows.append(row)
            a_cols_dw.append(idx_dw % fx.Int32(TILE_K // 4))
            # sorted_ids: token id in the low 24 bits, topk slot in the high 8.
            fused = fx.Int32(_global_i32_at(arg_mind, bx_m + row))
            a_row_base_dw.append((fused & fx.Int32(0x00FFFFFF)) * fx.Int32(K // 4))

        def store_a_tile(base_k):
            base_k_dw = base_k // fx.Int32(4)
            for i in range_constexpr(A_LOADS):
                col_bytes = a_cols_dw[i] * fx.Int32(4)
                g_byte = (a_row_base_dw[i] + base_k_dw) * fx.Int32(4) + _swizzle(
                    a_rows[i], col_bytes
                )
                l_byte = a_rows[i] * fx.Int32(TILE_K) + col_bytes
                r = fx.make_rmem_tensor(fx.make_layout(4, 1), fx.Int32)
                fx.copy(x_atom, fx.slice(x_tiles, (None, g_byte // fx.Int32(16))), r)
                fx.copy(
                    lds_write_atom,
                    r,
                    fx.slice(lds_tiles16, (None, l_byte // fx.Int32(16))),
                )

        def load_a(mi, ku):
            # Lane L of K-step ku holds row L%16, K = (ku//4)*128 + (L//16)*32 + (ku%4)*8.
            row = lane_mod_16 + fx.Int32(mi * 16)
            col = lane_div_16 * fx.Int32(32) + fx.Int32((ku // 4) * 128 + (ku % 4) * 8)
            off = row * fx.Int32(TILE_K) + _swizzle(row, col)
            r = fx.make_rmem_tensor(fx.make_layout(2, 1), fx.Int32)
            fx.copy_atom_call(
                lds_read_atom, fx.slice(lds_tiles8, (None, off // fx.Int32(8))), r
            )
            return fx.Vector(fx.memref_load_vec(r)).bitcast(fx.Float8E4M3FNUZ)

        # ---- W columns: wave owns TILE_N/4 gate cols (+ the matching up cols) ---
        def w_col(n0):
            # n0: 16-aligned W row (expert-flattened). Returns (16-row block,
            # 32-row scale block, npack half within the scale dword).
            return n0 // fx.Int32(16), n0 // fx.Int32(32), (n0 // fx.Int32(16)) % fx.Int32(2)

        n_wave_base = wave * fx.Int32(TILE_N // NUM_WAVES)
        out_cols, gate_cols, up_cols = [], [], []
        for ni in range_constexpr(N_REPEAT):
            n_local = by_n + n_wave_base + fx.Int32(ni * 16)
            out_cols.append(n_local + lane_mod_16)
            gate_cols.append(w_col(expert_off + n_local))
            up_cols.append(w_col(expert_off + n_local + inter_i32))

        # Per-output-channel max e8m0 exponent of this lane's gate / up column.
        exp_gate = [
            fx.Int32(_global_i32_at(arg_w_exp, expert_off + c)) for c in out_cols
        ]
        exp_up = [
            fx.Int32(_global_i32_at(arg_w_exp, expert_off + inter_i32 + c))
            for c in out_cols
        ]

        def load_w_raw(base_k, col):
            # raw[g][j]: i32 with 8 fp4 for K-step g*4 + j.
            n_blk = col[0]
            raw = []
            for g in range_constexpr(K_GROUPS):
                k0 = (base_k + fx.Int32(g * 128)) // fx.Int32(128)
                idx = fx.Int32(
                    crd2idx(
                        [
                            fx.Int64(n_blk),
                            fx.Int64(k0),
                            fx.Int64(lane_div_16),
                            fx.Int64(lane_mod_16),
                            fx.Int64(0),
                        ],
                        layout_w,
                    )
                )
                r = fx.make_rmem_tensor(fx.make_layout(4, 1), fx.Int32)
                fx.copy(w_atom, fx.slice(w_tiles, (None, idx // fx.Int32(16))), r)
                v4 = fx.Vector(fx.memref_load_vec(r))
                raw.append([fx.Int32(v4[j]) for j in range(4)])
            return raw

        def load_w_scale(base_k, col):
            # codes[g]: this lane's e8m0 byte for 128-K group g (shared by its 4 K-steps).
            _, sc_blk, sc_pack = col
            codes = []
            for g in range_constexpr(K_GROUPS):
                k32 = base_k // fx.Int32(32) + fx.Int32(g * 4) + lane_div_16
                idx = (
                    sc_blk * fx.Int32(SC_STRIDE_N0)
                    + (k32 // fx.Int32(8)) * fx.Int32(64)
                    + lane_div_16 * fx.Int32(16)
                    + lane_mod_16
                )
                packed = _buffer_i32_scalar_read(ws_tiles, idx, ws_atom)
                byte = ((k32 // fx.Int32(4)) % fx.Int32(2)) * fx.Int32(2) + sc_pack
                codes.append(packed.shrui(byte * fx.Int32(8)) & fx.Int32(0xFF))
            return codes

        def load_w_tile(base_k):
            g_sc = [load_w_scale(base_k, c) for c in gate_cols]
            u_sc = [load_w_scale(base_k, c) for c in up_cols]
            g_raw = [load_w_raw(base_k, c) for c in gate_cols]
            u_raw = [load_w_raw(base_k, c) for c in up_cols]
            return g_raw, u_raw, g_sc, u_sc

        # ---- accumulators -----------------------------------------------------
        acc_layout = fx.make_layout(4, 1)
        acc_gate = [
            [fx.make_rmem_tensor(acc_layout, fx.Float32) for _ in range(N_REPEAT)]
            for _ in range(M_REPEAT)
        ]
        acc_up = [
            [fx.make_rmem_tensor(acc_layout, fx.Float32) for _ in range(N_REPEAT)]
            for _ in range(M_REPEAT)
        ]
        zero4 = fx.Vector.filled(4, 0.0, fx.Float32)
        for mi in range_constexpr(M_REPEAT):
            for ni in range_constexpr(N_REPEAT):
                acc_gate[mi][ni].store(zero4)
                acc_up[mi][ni].store(zero4)

        mma_atom = fx.make_mma_atom(fx.rocdl.MFMA(16, 16, 32, fx.Float8E4M3FNUZ))

        def compute_tile(w_tile, a_frags):
            g_raw, u_raw, g_sc, u_sc = w_tile
            for ni in range_constexpr(N_REPEAT):
                g_lut = [
                    _fp8_lut(g_sc[ni][q], exp_gate[ni], flush_tiny)
                    for q in range_constexpr(K_GROUPS)
                ]
                u_lut = [
                    _fp8_lut(u_sc[ni][q], exp_up[ni], flush_tiny)
                    for q in range_constexpr(K_GROUPS)
                ]
                for ku in range_constexpr(K_STEPS):
                    gb = _fp4x8_to_fp8x8(g_raw[ni][ku // 4][ku % 4], g_lut[ku // 4])
                    ub = _fp4x8_to_fp8x8(u_raw[ni][ku // 4][ku % 4], u_lut[ku // 4])
                    for mi in range_constexpr(M_REPEAT):
                        a8 = a_frags[mi][ku]
                        _mma_fp8(mma_atom, acc_gate[mi][ni], a8, gb)
                        _mma_fp8(mma_atom, acc_up[mi][ni], a8, ub)

        # ---- main K loop: runtime scf.for, one A-LDS slot, no cross-tile prefetch
        # range() lowers to scf.for only inside an AST-rewritten (@flyc.jit) function;
        # accumulators are rmem tensors mutated in place, so no iter_args.
        @flyc.jit
        def _k_loop(k_base):
            for kt in range(K_TILES):
                base_k = k_base + fx.Int32(kt) * fx.Int32(TILE_K)
                store_a_tile(base_k)
                w_tile = load_w_tile(base_k)
                rocdl.s_waitcnt(lgkmcnt=0)
                gpu.barrier()  # A(kt) visible in LDS
                a_frags = [
                    [load_a(mi, ku) for ku in range_constexpr(K_STEPS)]
                    for mi in range_constexpr(M_REPEAT)
                ]
                compute_tile(w_tile, a_frags)
                gpu.barrier()  # all reads done before next tile overwrites the slot

        _k_loop(fx.Int32(0))

        # ---- epilogue: dequant -> SiLU(gate)*up -> bf16 by sorted position ------
        xs_tiles = _global_i32_buffer_tiles(
            arg_x_scale, fx.Int64(i32_ntok) * fx.Int64(4), 1
        )
        xs_atom = fx.make_copy_atom(fx.rocdl.BufferCopy32b(), fx.Int32)
        f_gate = [_channel_factor(x) for x in exp_gate]
        f_up = [_channel_factor(x) for x in exp_up]
        for mi in range_constexpr(M_REPEAT):
            for ii in range_constexpr(4):
                row_in_tile = (
                    fx.Int32(mi * 16) + lane_div_16 * fx.Int32(4) + fx.Int32(ii)
                )
                sorted_row = bx_m + row_in_tile
                fused = fx.Int32(_global_i32_at(arg_mind, sorted_row))
                token = fused & fx.Int32(0x00FFFFFF)
                valid = token < i32_ntok  # padding rows carry a sentinel token id
                rs = _buffer_i32_scalar_read(xs_tiles, token, xs_atom).bitcast(
                    fx.Float32
                )
                for ni in range_constexpr(N_REPEAT):
                    g = fx.Float32(fx.Vector(fx.memref_load_vec(acc_gate[mi][ni]))[ii])
                    u = fx.Float32(fx.Vector(fx.memref_load_vec(acc_up[mi][ni]))[ii])
                    g = g * (rs * f_gate[ni])
                    u = u * (rs * f_up[ni])
                    y = silu_mul_batch([g], [u])[0]
                    out_idx = sorted_row * inter_i32 + out_cols[ni]
                    buffer_ops.buffer_store(
                        y.to(fx.BFloat16), _raw(out_rsrc), _raw(out_idx), mask=valid
                    )

    @fx.struct
    class SharedStorage:
        raw: fx.Array[fx.Uint8, LDS_BYTES, 16]

    @flyc.jit
    def _entry(
        arg_x,
        arg_x_scale,
        arg_w,
        arg_w_scale,
        arg_w_exp,
        arg_eids,
        arg_cumsum,
        arg_mind,
        arg_out,
        i32_ntok,
    ):
        lds_ptr = fx.SharedAllocator().allocate(SharedStorage).peek().raw.ptr
        tx = fx.Int32(gpu.thread_id("x"))
        bx = fx.Int32(gpu.block_id("x"))
        lane = tx % fx.Int32(64)
        wave = rocdl.readfirstlane(T.i32, tx // fx.Int32(64))
        cumsum0 = _global_i32_at(arg_cumsum, fx.Int32(0))
        total_m_blocks = cumsum0 // fx.Int32(BM)
        bound = total_m_blocks * fx.Int32(NUM_N_BLOCKS)

        # Bijective XCD round-robin over valid tiles; xcd_swizzle>0 also groups
        # xcd_swizzle m-blocks per XCD for L2 locality.
        NXCD = 8
        xq = _udiv(bound, NXCD)
        xr = _umod(bound, NXCD)

        def _xcd(pid):
            xc = _umod(pid, NXCD)
            wgid = xc * xq + fx.min(xc, xr) + _udiv(pid, NXCD)
            ng = fx.Int32(xcd_swizzle * NUM_N_BLOCKS)
            first_m = (wgid // ng) * fx.Int32(xcd_swizzle)
            group_m = fx.min(total_m_blocks - first_m, fx.Int32(xcd_swizzle))
            wig = wgid % ng
            return (first_m + wig % group_m) * fx.Int32(NUM_N_BLOCKS) + wig // group_m

        if bx < bound:
            if const_expr(xcd_swizzle > 0):
                tile = _xcd(bx)
            else:
                tile = bx
            _body(
                lds_ptr,
                arg_x,
                arg_x_scale,
                arg_w,
                arg_w_scale,
                arg_w_exp,
                arg_eids,
                arg_cumsum,
                arg_mind,
                arg_out,
                i32_ntok,
                tile,
                lane,
                wave,
            )

    @flyc.kernel(name=kname, known_block_size=[256, 1, 1])
    def a8w4_gemm1_kernel(
        arg_x: fx.Int64,
        arg_x_scale: fx.Int64,
        arg_w: fx.Int64,
        arg_w_scale: fx.Int64,
        arg_w_exp: fx.Int64,
        arg_eids: fx.Int64,
        arg_cumsum: fx.Int64,
        arg_mind: fx.Int64,
        arg_out: fx.Int64,
        i32_ntok: fx.Int32,
    ):
        _entry(
            arg_x,
            arg_x_scale,
            arg_w,
            arg_w_scale,
            arg_w_exp,
            arg_eids,
            arg_cumsum,
            arg_mind,
            arg_out,
            i32_ntok,
        )

    @flyc.jit
    def launch(
        arg_x: fx.Int64,
        arg_x_scale: fx.Int64,
        arg_w: fx.Int64,
        arg_w_scale: fx.Int64,
        arg_w_exp: fx.Int64,
        arg_eids: fx.Int64,
        arg_cumsum: fx.Int64,
        arg_mind: fx.Int64,
        arg_out: fx.Int64,
        i32_ntok: fx.Int32,
        i32_grid: fx.Int32,
        stream: fx.Stream,
    ):
        a8w4_gemm1_kernel(
            arg_x,
            arg_x_scale,
            arg_w,
            arg_w_scale,

def run_torch(
    x_fp8, x_scale, w1_qt, w1_scale, sorted_ids, sorted_expert_ids, num_valid_ids, tile_m
):
    """fp32 reference in the kernel's sorted output layout.

    Uses the same FP8 A (dequantized with its row scale) and exact mxfp4 W, so the
    only differences are accumulation order and the bf16 output rounding.
    Returns (ref bf16 [sorted_size, inter], mask of rows the kernel writes).
    """
    tokens, model_dim = x_fp8.shape
    E, n_out, _ = w1_qt.shape
    inter_dim = n_out // 2
    sorted_size = sorted_expert_ids.numel() * tile_m
    nv = int(num_valid_ids[0].item())

    ids = sorted_ids[:nv].to(torch.int64)
    token = ids & 0x00FFFFFF
    row_expert = sorted_expert_ids.to(torch.int64).repeat_interleave(tile_m)[:nv]
    valid = token < tokens
    mask = torch.zeros(sorted_size, dtype=torch.bool, device=x_fp8.device)
    mask[:nv] = valid

    a = x_fp8.to(torch.float32) * x_scale.view(-1, 1)
    w_scale = fp4_utils.e8m0_to_f32(w1_scale).view(E, n_out, model_dim // 32, 1)
    ref = torch.zeros((sorted_size, inter_dim), dtype=torch.float32, device=a.device)
    for e in row_expert[valid].unique().tolist():
        rows = torch.nonzero(valid & (row_expert == e)).squeeze(1)
        w = fp4_utils.mxfp4_to_f32(w1_qt[e]).view(n_out, model_dim // 32, 32)
        w = (w * w_scale[e]).view(n_out, model_dim)
        gate, up = (a[token[rows]] @ w.t()).split(inter_dim, dim=-1)
        ref[rows] = F.silu(gate) * up
    return ref.to(dtypes.bf16), mask


def _cos_diff(x, y):
    x, y = x.double(), y.double()
    return float(1 - 2 * (x * y).sum() / (x * x + y * y).sum())

Since only about 1.7 waves fit per SIMD, latency hiding is weak, making prefetching the key optimization lever—overlapping loads with compute within a single wave rather than relying on more waves to hide latency. The VALU+MFMA work seems to leave each unit roughly 40-50% busy given the wave count, confirming there's room to exploit better overlap rather than adding more parallelism.

These savings aren't linearly additive once memory is hidden — after prefetching, per-iteration cost drops to roughly 3.5-4k cycles from the VALU+MFMA reduction, at which point the kernel becomes HBM-bound. Working through the math on 285MB at achievable bandwidth suggests a realistic target of ~70-80us down from 116us, a 30-40% overall speedup, so now I want to verify my VGPR count assumption by checking the actual compiled code object files for the register usage metadata.

根据 trace（dispatch 6005，即 `a8w4_gemm1_h4096_i256_ne256_bm64_tn128_tk256_bcm1_xcd0_ftz`）和几组 tile 实测，缺省参数下估计还有 **30–40% 的优化空间**（约 115us → 70–80us）。其中最直接的一项不用改代码：把 tile_m 从 64 改成 32，实测就能快 13–15%。

## 现状

**整体情况**
- **grid**：tile_m=64 时共 256 个 m-block，每个 m-block 拆成 2 个 n-block，合计 512 个 WG，分到 304 个 CU 上只有一轮。其中 208 个 CU 跑 2 个 WG，96 个 CU 跑 1 个。
- **padding**：每个 expert 平均只有 16 个 token（最少 7、最多 29），而 tile_m=64，所以 75% 的行是 padding。16 行一组的子块里只有 368/1024（36%）有有效数据。
- **寄存器**：VGPR 172、AGPR 0、LDS 16KB，所以每个 SIMD 最多 2 个 wave。
  - 原 port 版本是 166 个 VGPR，能放 3 个 wave。我抽取时把用量推过了 168 这条线，可以放回 3 个 wave，后面要修回来。
  - 当前 shape 每个 CU 只有约 1.7 个 WG，这一点暂时不影响；到 prefill（每个 CU 有 3 个以上 WG）时会影响。
- **wave 耗时**：每个 wave 约 155k–194k cycle。和别的 wave 共享 SIMD 的 wave（slot1）要多花约 15%。
- **带宽**：权重和 scale 共约 285MB。按 MI300X 实际能跑到约 4 TB/s 算，下限大约 70us；现在约 115us，只有 2.5 TB/s。

**每个 wave 每次 K 迭代的时间分布**（latency 总和除以 448 = 28 个 wave × 16 次迭代）

| 项 | cycle/iter | 占比 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `s_waitcnt vmcnt` | 约 2.9k | 约 28% | `vmcnt(8)` 750k、`vmcnt(4)` 259k、`vmcnt(1)` 243k |
| VALU（fp4→fp8 解码） | 3.3k | 31.6% | 每次迭代约 600 条 VALU，对应 128 条 MFMA |
| MFMA | 1.6k | 15.6% | 其中 64% 算的是全 padding 的子块 |
| `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt` | 约 0.9k | 约 8% | `ds_read` 后立刻等 |
| `buffer_load` 发射 | 0.77k | 7.3% | |
| `s_barrier` ×2 | 0.58k | 5.5% | |
| `s_nop` + 其他 | 约 0.3k | 约 2% | |

trace 里还有一个新现象：编译器因为寄存器压力，把 8 条 W load 中的 3 条推迟到了解码之后才发（地址 7964–7984）。这导致计算做到一半时在 `vmcnt(1)` 处又卡了 243k。

## 优化空间（按收益/成本排序）

| # | 手段 | 依据 | 预估收益 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **改用 tile_m=32**（不用改代码） | 最多的 expert 也只有 29 个 token，每个 expert 仍然只占一个 block，权重读取量不变，MFMA、A 搬运和累加器减半。现在 fp8r 的配置注册表里只有 tile_m 64/128，没有 32 | **实测 −13~15%**（112–118us → 97–102us） |
| 2 | **跨迭代预取**：runtime 循环里先发 kt+1 的 W、scale 和 A，再算 kt；A 的 LDS 改成双缓冲，每次迭代只留一个 barrier | 显存等待约 28%、barrier 5.5%，当前算和取完全串行。这个 shape 每个 SIMD 本来只有 1.7 个 wave，多用约 50 个 VGPR（总数不超过 256）不会降低并发；LDS 2×16KB 也放得下 2 个 WG | **−20~30%**，最大的一项 |
| 3 | **解码精简**：ftz 打开时，离线把 −0 nibble 规范成 +0；sign mask 和 LUT 一起计算（flush 时为 0）；去掉 `zeros` 修正 | 每个 fragment 的解码从约 16 条 VALU 降到约 10 条，结果和现在完全一致 | VALU −35%，约 **−8~10%**；预取做完后会更明显 |
| 4 | **跳过全 padding 的 16 行子块**：每个 wave 先根据 sorted_ids 算出每个子块有没有有效行，再用统一分支跳过对应的 MFMA 和 `ds_read` | tile_m=64 时只有 36% 的子块非空，tile_m=32 时 72% | tile_m=64 时 −8~10%；和第 1 项叠加后约 −3% |
| 5 | 修回 VGPR ≤168 | 恢复每 SIMD 3 个 wave | 当前 shape 没收益；prefill 大 token 时需要 |
| 6 | 把 `ds_read` 集中先发、再分段等 `lgkmcnt(N)`；用无关 VALU 去填 `s_nop` | lgkmcnt 约 8%、nop 0.9% | −3~5% |

其他结论：
- **改 TILE_N 解决不了负载不均**：tile_n=64 实测和 128 差不多（约 94–98us）。每个 WG 的耗时主要是 16 次串行迭代的延迟，而不是吞吐。
- **测量噪声**：同一配置多次跑会差约 ±4%。上面的结论都基于至少两次测量。

## 建议路线
1. 先在 fp8r 的注册表里加上 tile_m 32（以及 16），重新 tune。代价最小，能拿到 −13%。
2. 给 `compile_a8w4_gemm1` 的 runtime 循环加预取和 A 的 LDS 双缓冲。重点看 `vmcnt` 的 stall 能不能压到 0.5k cycle/iter 以下。
3. 做解码精简（第 3 项）和 padding 子块跳过（第 4 项）。
4. 最后核对 VGPR，并用 4096 以上的 token 回归测试 prefill 场景。

全部做完，目标约 70–80us，相当于 3.6–4 TB/s，接近显存带宽上限。

response.value:
I see the issue now: the compiler is scheduling the prefetch loads too late, deep into the compute section after most of the MFMAs have already issued. That means the waitcnt at the top of the loop ends up blocking on loads that were issued near the end of the previous iteration, so there's no real overlap between memory and compute — each iteration effectively stalls for the full load latency instead of hiding it.

To fix this I need to force the scheduler to keep those loads early rather than letting it reorder things. I'm checking whether the dialect exposes scheduling barrier intrinsics — things like sched_barrier, s_setprio, or sched_group_barrier — that I can insert to pin instruction ordering.

The noise might be from warm-up ordering or GPU contention with another user rather than the timing overhead itself. I should write a bench script that alternates candidates multiple times and takes the minimum to get more robust comparisons.

For the actual bench, I'll just rerun the test repeating the same tile several times via `--tile 32,128 32,128 32,128` and take the min across runs — the data generation cost is acceptable overhead.

Now I'm digging into the VGPR blow-up at 254: the expected count from accumulators, fragments, and weight/activation buffers only adds up to around 150, so something's forcing the compiler to hoist decode operations for all fragments ahead of the MFMAs, likely interacting with the sched_barrier regions since it dropped to 140 without that barrier. I want to check whether read_w() ordering relative to the loads is causing extra live ranges, so I'm going to look at the actual ISA structure of the loop to pin down where the extra VGPRs come from.

VGPR usage at 254 keeps us at 2 waves/SIMD, which is acceptable for this shape, though I'm noticing the epilogue has some vmcnt(0) waits worth checking.

These stem from scale loads interleaved between stores — each epilogue row reads sorted_ids and x_scale, so there's a wait per row, but this is minor since it only happens once. Now I should measure this robustly; since bench_a8w4_gemm1 rebuilds data (1GB randn plus quantization) each run, it's slow, so I'll just run across several tile configurations and compare results directly rather than building a separate harness.

Looking at 15 loop iterations, I'm trying to figure out why buffer_load issue is stalling for roughly 400-500 cycles each, which adds up to about 2458 cycles per iteration. With 12 loads happening per iteration, I suspect this is a VGPR hazard where loads writing into registers conflict with in-flight reads rather than simply the issue queue being full.

I'm now wondering if it's really the TA/TD queue filling up because all waves fire their loads simultaneously right after the barrier, compared to the original kernel's much lower 765 cycles per iteration. Looking more closely at register allocation, it seems the compiler may be reusing the same physical VGPRs (v[0:3]) for both the old W(kt) values and the new load destinations, which means it has to guarantee the old values are fully consumed before the new load can land — and tracing the instruction order, the VALU decode happens before the barrier and loads, so this reuse could be forcing a wait that explains the stall.

Computing effective memory throughput, I get around 2.9TB/s against a 5.3TB/s HBM peak, and the fact that vmcnt is still waiting ~935 cycles per iteration at the loop top suggests the loads aren't finishing even after the whole compute phase — pointing toward the memory system's queues being saturated rather than compute being the bottleneck now.

I'm checking whether the W dwordx4 loads are properly coalesced: with lanes addressing in a pattern of intra-group offset plus klane stride, 64 lanes cover a contiguous 1KB block, which looks correctly coalesced, while the A loads are gathering rows instead. With glc/sc0 caching mode, the 2.9TB/s figure might actually be near the practical ceiling given limited memory-level parallelism — only around 1.7 workgroups per CU in flight, so I'm estimating per-CU in-flight memory traffic per iteration based on the W tile size.

Working through the math, roughly 40KB per workgroup times 1.7 WGs times 304 CUs gives about 20MB in flight, which by Little's Law would suggest ~10TB/s potential at a few microseconds of latency — so this shouldn't be MLP-limited in theory. But since the vmcnt at the top of each iteration isn't clearing, I suspect HBM latency climbs to 3-5µs under saturation, and the buffer_load stalls likely indicate the TA request queue itself is filling up with limited depth.

This looks like straightforward bandwidth saturation rather than an MLP issue — 12 loads across 4 waves and 2 workgroups means ~96 in-flight requests, which is typical for bandwidth-bound kernels at this point. I want to verify the actual achievable peak against the 2.9TB/s figure by testing a simple copy-like read at the same size, and also try sweeping the cache modifier settings (sc0/nt variations) to see if that changes throughput, plus double-check the kernel's wave span and cycle count to make sure the timing numbers line up.

Now I'm seeing it's load imbalance across the 304 CUs: 208 CUs get 2 workgroups while 96 get only 1, so the single-workgroup CUs sit idle after finishing, dragging down bandwidth utilization during the tail — total runtime essentially tracks the 2-workgroup CUs' duration. I'm considering fixes like shrinking tile size to rebalance work more evenly, but that runs into VGPR occupancy limits capping concurrent workgroups per CU, so I'd need to cut VGPR usage further to allow more workgroups per CU, or explore split-K, or a persistent kernel with work-stealing instead.

# (``_channel_factor``, applied in the epilogue); per 32-K group the remaining
# 2**(5-delta), delta = max_exp - group_exp, is folded into an 8-entry
# E2M1-magnitude -> FP8-FNUZ byte table (``_fp8_lut``) so each nibble decodes with
# one v_perm.


def _perm_u32(hi, lo, sel):
    return fx.Uint32(
        rocdl.perm_b32(
            fx.Uint32(hi).ir_value(), fx.Uint32(lo).ir_value(), fx.Uint32(sel).ir_value()
        )
    )


def _fp8_lut(group_code, max_code, flush_tiny):
    """8-entry ``|E2M1| * 2**(5-delta)`` -> FP8-FNUZ byte table, as (lo, hi) dwords.

    ``group_code`` is the 32-K group's E8M0 byte, ``max_code`` the channel max.
    Includes RNE subnormals for delta in 12..18; delta >= 19 rounds to zero.
    """
    difference = max_code - group_code
    delta = fx.min(difference, 11).to(fx.Uint32) * fx.Uint32(0x08080808)
    lo = (fx.Uint32(0x6C686080) - delta) & fx.Uint32(0xFFFFFF00)
    hi = fx.Uint32(0x7C787470) - delta
    if const_expr(flush_tiny):
        # Approximation: drop groups < 2**-11 of this channel's largest scale.
        return (
            (difference > 11).select(fx.Uint32(0), lo),
            (difference > 11).select(fx.Uint32(0), hi),
        )
    for diff, low, high in (
        (12, 0x0C080400, 0x1C181410),
        (13, 0x06040200, 0x14100C08),
        (14, 0x03020100, 0x0C080604),
        (15, 0x02010000, 0x06040302),
        (16, 0x01000000, 0x03020201),
        (17, 0, 0x02010100),
        (18, 0, 0x01000000),
    ):
        lo = (difference == diff).select(fx.Uint32(low), lo)
        hi = (difference == diff).select(fx.Uint32(high), hi)
    lo = (difference >= 19).select(fx.Uint32(0), lo)
    hi = (difference >= 19).select(fx.Uint32(0), hi)
    return lo, hi


def _fp4x8_to_fp8x8(raw, lut):
    """Eight consecutive FP4 nibbles (one i32) -> v8 FP8-FNUZ MFMA operand."""
    raw = fx.Uint32(raw)
    low, high = lut
    even = _perm_u32(high, low, raw & 0x07070707)  # nibbles 0,2,4,6
    odd = _perm_u32(high, low, (raw >> 4) & 0x07070707)  # nibbles 1,3,5,7
    parts = []
    for mag, sign in (
        (even, (raw & 0x08080808) << 4),
        (odd, raw & fx.Uint32(0x80808080)),
    ):
        # FNUZ has no -0 (0x80 is NaN): clear the sign of zero-magnitude bytes.
        zeros = (~(mag + fx.Uint32(0x7F7F7F7F))) & fx.Uint32(0x80808080)
        parts.append((mag | sign) & ~zeros)
    lo = _perm_u32(parts[1], parts[0], 0x05010400).bitcast(fx.Int32)
    hi = _perm_u32(parts[1], parts[0], 0x07030602).bitcast(fx.Int32)
    return fx.Vector.from_elements([lo, hi], fx.Int32).bitcast(fx.Float8E4M3FNUZ)


def _channel_factor(exponent):
    """2**(exponent-127-5) as f32 (subnormal-safe)."""
    normal = ((exponent - 5).to(fx.Uint32) << 23).bitcast(fx.Float32)
    subnormal = (fx.Uint32(1) << (exponent + 17).to(fx.Uint32)).bitcast(fx.Float32)
    return (exponent >= 6).select(normal, subnormal)


def _fp8_frag8(v8):
    t = fx.make_rmem_tensor(fx.make_layout(8, 1), fx.Float8E4M3FNUZ)
    t.store(v8)
    return t


def _mma_fp8(mma_atom, acc, a8, b8):
    """acc += A(16x32) * B(32x16), one MFMA(16,16,32,fp8 FNUZ)."""
    fx.gemm(mma_atom, acc, _fp8_frag8(a8), _fp8_frag8(b8), acc)

# Kernel
# =============================================================================


@functools.cache
def compile_a8w4_gemm1(
    *,
    D_HIDDEN,
    D_INTER,
    NE,
    BM=64,
    TILE_N=128,
    TILE_K=256,
    b_cache_mod=1,
    xcd_swizzle=0,
    waves_per_eu=None,
    flush_tiny=True,
):
    """Build the A8W4 stage1 launcher.

    Launch args (raw device pointers): ``x`` fp8 [tokens, K], ``x_scale`` f32
    [tokens], ``w`` mxfp4 [E, 2*inter, K/2] (standard preshuffle), ``w_scale`` e8m0
    (shuffled), ``w_exp`` int32 [E, 2*inter] (``channel_exponents``),
    ``sorted_expert_ids``, ``num_valid_ids``, ``sorted_ids``, ``out`` bf16
    [sorted_size, inter], then ``tokens``, ``grid`` and the stream.
    """
    K = D_HIDDEN
    INTER = D_INTER
    N_OUT = 2 * INTER  # gate | up
    NUM_WAVES = 4
    assert K % TILE_K == 0 and TILE_K % 128 == 0, f"bad K={K} / TILE_K={TILE_K}"
    assert N_OUT % 256 == 0, f"2*inter_dim must be a multiple of 256, got {N_OUT}"
    assert INTER % TILE_N == 0, f"inter_dim must be a multiple of TILE_N={TILE_N}"
    assert TILE_N % (NUM_WAVES * 16) == 0, f"TILE_N must be a multiple of 64"
    assert BM % 16 == 0, f"BM must be a multiple of 16, got {BM}"
    assert (BM * TILE_K) % (256 * 16) == 0, "A tile must be whole 16 B per thread"

    NUM_N_BLOCKS = INTER // TILE_N
    K_TILES = K // TILE_K
    M_REPEAT = BM // 16  # 16-row MFMA blocks per tile
    N_REPEAT = TILE_N // NUM_WAVES // 16  # 16-col MFMA blocks per wave (gate and up)
    K_STEPS = TILE_K // 32  # MFMA K32 steps per tile
    K_GROUPS = TILE_K // 128  # 128-K groups: one W dwordx4 + one scale dword each
    A_LOADS = BM * TILE_K // (256 * 16)  # 16 B A copies per thread per tile
    LDS_BYTES = BM * TILE_K  # fp8 A tile, single slot

    # W (mxfp4) N-major preshuffle in bytes: (N/16, K/128, klane=4, nlane=16, kpack=16).
    W_K0 = K // 128
    W_BYTES = NE * N_OUT * K // 2
    # E8M0 scale preshuffle (dwords): (N/32, Kpad/256, klane=4, nlane=16); each dword
    # packs [kpack=2] x [npack=2] bytes.
    SCALE_K_PAD = ((K + 255) // 256) * 256
    SC_STRIDE_N0 = (SCALE_K_PAD // 256) * 64
    WS_BYTES = NE * N_OUT * (SCALE_K_PAD // 32)

    ftz_tag = "_ftz" if flush_tiny else ""
    wpe_tag = f"_w{waves_per_eu}" if waves_per_eu else ""
    kname = (
        f"a8w4_gemm1_h{K}_i{INTER}_ne{NE}_bm{BM}_tn{TILE_N}_tk{TILE_K}"
        f"_bcm{b_cache_mod}_xcd{xcd_swizzle}{wpe_tag}{ftz_tag}"
    )

    def _body(
        lds_ptr,
        arg_x,
        arg_x_scale,
        arg_w,
        arg_w_scale,
        arg_w_exp,
        arg_eids,
        arg_cumsum,
        arg_mind,
        arg_out,
        i32_ntok,
        tile,
        lane,
        wave,
    ):
        lane_div_16 = lane // fx.Int32(16)
        lane_mod_16 = lane % fx.Int32(16)

        # ---- tile decode: m-block (one expert) x n-block (inter tile) ----------
        n_block = tile % fx.Int32(NUM_N_BLOCKS)
        m_block = tile // fx.Int32(NUM_N_BLOCKS)
        e = rocdl.readfirstlane(T.i32, _raw(_global_i32_at(arg_eids, m_block)))
        bx_m = m_block * fx.Int32(BM)  # first sorted row of this m-block
        by_n = n_block * fx.Int32(TILE_N)
        inter_i32 = fx.Int32(INTER)

        # ---- W operand resources ------------------------------------------------
        expert_off = e * fx.Int32(N_OUT)
        layout_w = fx.make_layout(
            (N_OUT // 16, W_K0, 4, 16, 16), (W_K0 * 1024, 1024, 256, 16, 1)
        )
        w_tiles = _global_i32_buffer_tiles(arg_w, min(W_BYTES, 0xFFFFFFFF), 4)
        w_atom = fx.make_copy_atom(fx.rocdl.BufferCopy128b(b_cache_mod), fx.Int32)
        ws_tiles = _global_i32_buffer_tiles(arg_w_scale, min(WS_BYTES, 0xFFFFFFFF), 1)
        ws_atom = fx.make_copy_atom(fx.rocdl.BufferCopy32b(0), fx.Int32)

        # ---- output resource: [cumsum0, INTER] bf16, OOB stores are dropped -----
        cumsum0 = _global_i32_at(arg_cumsum, fx.Int32(0))
        out_rsrc = buffer_ops.create_buffer_resource_from_addr(
            _raw(fx.Int64(arg_out)),
            num_records_bytes=_raw(fx.Int64(cumsum0) * fx.Int64(INTER * 2)),
        )

        # ---- A operand: gather BM sorted rows of x -> LDS (via VGPRs on gfx942) -
        # Extent = the real [tokens, K] alloc so padding rows (token >= tokens) read 0.
        x_tiles = fx.logical_divide(
            _global_i32_buffer_view(
                arg_x, fx.Int64(i32_ntok) * fx.Int64(K // 4) * fx.Int64(4)
            ),
            fx.make_layout(4, 1),
        )
        x_atom = fx.make_copy_atom(fx.rocdl.BufferCopy128b(2), fx.Int32)
        lds_flat = fx.make_view(
            fx.recast_iter(fx.Int32, lds_ptr), fx.make_layout(LDS_BYTES // 4, 1)
        )
        lds_tiles16 = fx.logical_divide(lds_flat, fx.make_layout(4, 1))
        lds_tiles8 = fx.logical_divide(lds_flat, fx.make_layout(2, 1))
        lds_write_atom = fx.make_copy_atom(fx.UniversalCopy128b(), fx.Int32)
        lds_read_atom = fx.make_copy_atom(fx.UniversalCopy64b(), fx.Int32)

        def _swizzle(row, col_bytes):
            # A-LDS bank-conflict XOR swizzle; applied to the GMEM source column on
            # the write (LDS destination linear) and to the LDS column on the read.
            return col_bytes ^ ((row & fx.Int32(TILE_K // 16 - 1)) * fx.Int32(16))

        tx = fx.Int32(gpu.thread_id("x"))
        a_rows, a_cols_dw, a_row_base_dw = [], [], []
        for i in range_constexpr(A_LOADS):
            idx_dw = tx * fx.Int32(4) + fx.Int32(i * 256 * 4)
            row = idx_dw // fx.Int32(TILE_K // 4)
            a_rows.append(row)
            a_cols_dw.append(idx_dw % fx.Int32(TILE_K // 4))
            # sorted_ids: token id in the low 24 bits, topk slot in the high 8.
            fused = fx.Int32(_global_i32_at(arg_mind, bx_m + row))
            a_row_base_dw.append((fused & fx.Int32(0x00FFFFFF)) * fx.Int32(K // 4))

        def store_a_tile(base_k):
            base_k_dw = base_k // fx.Int32(4)
            for i in range_constexpr(A_LOADS):
                col_bytes = a_cols_dw[i] * fx.Int32(4)
                g_byte = (a_row_base_dw[i] + base_k_dw) * fx.Int32(4) + _swizzle(
                    a_rows[i], col_bytes
                )
                l_byte = a_rows[i] * fx.Int32(TILE_K) + col_bytes
                r = fx.make_rmem_tensor(fx.make_layout(4, 1), fx.Int32)
                fx.copy(x_atom, fx.slice(x_tiles, (None, g_byte // fx.Int32(16))), r)
                fx.copy(
                    lds_write_atom,
                    r,
                    fx.slice(lds_tiles16, (None, l_byte // fx.Int32(16))),
                )

        def load_a(mi, ku):
            # Lane L of K-step ku holds row L%16, K = (ku//4)*128 + (L//16)*32 + (ku%4)*8.
            row = lane_mod_16 + fx.Int32(mi * 16)
            col = lane_div_16 * fx.Int32(32) + fx.Int32((ku // 4) * 128 + (ku % 4) * 8)
            off = row * fx.Int32(TILE_K) + _swizzle(row, col)
            r = fx.make_rmem_tensor(fx.make_layout(2, 1), fx.Int32)
            fx.copy_atom_call(
                lds_read_atom, fx.slice(lds_tiles8, (None, off // fx.Int32(8))), r
            )
            return fx.Vector(fx.memref_load_vec(r)).bitcast(fx.Float8E4M3FNUZ)

        # ---- W columns: wave owns TILE_N/4 gate cols (+ the matching up cols) ---
        def w_col(n0):
            # n0: 16-aligned W row (expert-flattened). Returns (16-row block,
            # 32-row scale block, npack half within the scale dword).
            return n0 // fx.Int32(16), n0 // fx.Int32(32), (n0 // fx.Int32(16)) % fx.Int32(2)

        n_wave_base = wave * fx.Int32(TILE_N // NUM_WAVES)
        out_cols, gate_cols, up_cols = [], [], []
        for ni in range_constexpr(N_REPEAT):
            n_local = by_n + n_wave_base + fx.Int32(ni * 16)
            out_cols.append(n_local + lane_mod_16)
            gate_cols.append(w_col(expert_off + n_local))
            up_cols.append(w_col(expert_off + n_local + inter_i32))

        # Per-output-channel max e8m0 exponent of this lane's gate / up column.
        exp_gate = [
            fx.Int32(_global_i32_at(arg_w_exp, expert_off + c)) for c in out_cols
        ]
        exp_up = [
            fx.Int32(_global_i32_at(arg_w_exp, expert_off + inter_i32 + c))
            for c in out_cols
        ]

        def load_w_raw(base_k, col):
            # raw[g][j]: i32 with 8 fp4 for K-step g*4 + j.
            n_blk = col[0]
            raw = []
            for g in range_constexpr(K_GROUPS):
                k0 = (base_k + fx.Int32(g * 128)) // fx.Int32(128)
                idx = fx.Int32(
                    crd2idx(
                        [
                            fx.Int64(n_blk),
                            fx.Int64(k0),
                            fx.Int64(lane_div_16),
                            fx.Int64(lane_mod_16),
                            fx.Int64(0),
                        ],
                        layout_w,
                    )
                )
                r = fx.make_rmem_tensor(fx.make_layout(4, 1), fx.Int32)
                fx.copy(w_atom, fx.slice(w_tiles, (None, idx // fx.Int32(16))), r)
                v4 = fx.Vector(fx.memref_load_vec(r))
                raw.append([fx.Int32(v4[j]) for j in range(4)])
            return raw

        def load_w_scale(base_k, col):
            # codes[g]: this lane's e8m0 byte for 128-K group g (shared by its 4 K-steps).
            _, sc_blk, sc_pack = col
            codes = []
            for g in range_constexpr(K_GROUPS):
                k32 = base_k // fx.Int32(32) + fx.Int32(g * 4) + lane_div_16
                idx = (
                    sc_blk * fx.Int32(SC_STRIDE_N0)
                    + (k32 // fx.Int32(8)) * fx.Int32(64)
                    + lane_div_16 * fx.Int32(16)
                    + lane_mod_16
                )
                packed = _buffer_i32_scalar_read(ws_tiles, idx, ws_atom)
                byte = ((k32 // fx.Int32(4)) % fx.Int32(2)) * fx.Int32(2) + sc_pack
                codes.append(packed.shrui(byte * fx.Int32(8)) & fx.Int32(0xFF))
            return codes

        def load_w_tile(base_k):
            g_sc = [load_w_scale(base_k, c) for c in gate_cols]
            u_sc = [load_w_scale(base_k, c) for c in up_cols]
            g_raw = [load_w_raw(base_k, c) for c in gate_cols]
            u_raw = [load_w_raw(base_k, c) for c in up_cols]
            return g_raw, u_raw, g_sc, u_sc

        # ---- accumulators -----------------------------------------------------
        acc_layout = fx.make_layout(4, 1)
        acc_gate = [
            [fx.make_rmem_tensor(acc_layout, fx.Float32) for _ in range(N_REPEAT)]
            for _ in range(M_REPEAT)
        ]
        acc_up = [
            [fx.make_rmem_tensor(acc_layout, fx.Float32) for _ in range(N_REPEAT)]
            for _ in range(M_REPEAT)
        ]
        zero4 = fx.Vector.filled(4, 0.0, fx.Float32)
        for mi in range_constexpr(M_REPEAT):
            for ni in range_constexpr(N_REPEAT):
                acc_gate[mi][ni].store(zero4)
                acc_up[mi][ni].store(zero4)

        mma_atom = fx.make_mma_atom(fx.rocdl.MFMA(16, 16, 32, fx.Float8E4M3FNUZ))

        def compute_tile(w_tile, a_frags):
            g_raw, u_raw, g_sc, u_sc = w_tile
            for ni in range_constexpr(N_REPEAT):
                g_lut = [
                    _fp8_lut(g_sc[ni][q], exp_gate[ni], flush_tiny)
                    for q in range_constexpr(K_GROUPS)
                ]
                u_lut = [
                    _fp8_lut(u_sc[ni][q], exp_up[ni], flush_tiny)
                    for q in range_constexpr(K_GROUPS)
                ]
                for ku in range_constexpr(K_STEPS):
                    gb = _fp4x8_to_fp8x8(g_raw[ni][ku // 4][ku % 4], g_lut[ku // 4])
                    ub = _fp4x8_to_fp8x8(u_raw[ni][ku // 4][ku % 4], u_lut[ku // 4])
                    for mi in range_constexpr(M_REPEAT):
                        a8 = a_frags[mi][ku]
                        _mma_fp8(mma_atom, acc_gate[mi][ni], a8, gb)
                        _mma_fp8(mma_atom, acc_up[mi][ni], a8, ub)

        # ---- main K loop: runtime scf.for, one A-LDS slot, no cross-tile prefetch
        # range() lowers to scf.for only inside an AST-rewritten (@flyc.jit) function;
        # accumulators are rmem tensors mutated in place, so no iter_args.
        @flyc.jit
        def _k_loop(k_base):
            for kt in range(K_TILES):
                base_k = k_base + fx.Int32(kt) * fx.Int32(TILE_K)
                store_a_tile(base_k)
                w_tile = load_w_tile(base_k)
                rocdl.s_waitcnt(lgkmcnt=0)
                gpu.barrier()  # A(kt) visible in LDS
                a_frags = [
                    [load_a(mi, ku) for ku in range_constexpr(K_STEPS)]
                    for mi in range_constexpr(M_REPEAT)
                ]
                compute_tile(w_tile, a_frags)
                gpu.barrier()  # all reads done before next tile overwrites the slot

        _k_loop(fx.Int32(0))

        # ---- epilogue: dequant -> SiLU(gate)*up -> bf16 by sorted position ------
        xs_tiles = _global_i32_buffer_tiles(
            arg_x_scale, fx.Int64(i32_ntok) * fx.Int64(4), 1
        )
        xs_atom = fx.make_copy_atom(fx.rocdl.BufferCopy32b(), fx.Int32)
        f_gate = [_channel_factor(x) for x in exp_gate]
        f_up = [_channel_factor(x) for x in exp_up]
        for mi in range_constexpr(M_REPEAT):
            for ii in range_constexpr(4):
                row_in_tile = (
                    fx.Int32(mi * 16) + lane_div_16 * fx.Int32(4) + fx.Int32(ii)
                )
                sorted_row = bx_m + row_in_tile
                fused = fx.Int32(_global_i32_at(arg_mind, sorted_row))
                token = fused & fx.Int32(0x00FFFFFF)
                valid = token < i32_ntok  # padding rows carry a sentinel token id
                rs = _buffer_i32_scalar_read(xs_tiles, token, xs_atom).bitcast(
                    fx.Float32
                )
                for ni in range_constexpr(N_REPEAT):
                    g = fx.Float32(fx.Vector(fx.memref_load_vec(acc_gate[mi][ni]))[ii])
                    u = fx.Float32(fx.Vector(fx.memref_load_vec(acc_up[mi][ni]))[ii])
                    g = g * (rs * f_gate[ni])
                    u = u * (rs * f_up[ni])
                    y = silu_mul_batch([g], [u])[0]
                    out_idx = sorted_row * inter_i32 + out_cols[ni]
                    buffer_ops.buffer_store(
                        y.to(fx.BFloat16), _raw(out_rsrc), _raw(out_idx), mask=valid
                    )

    @fx.struct
    class SharedStorage:
        raw: fx.Array[fx.Uint8, LDS_BYTES, 16]

    @flyc.jit
    def _entry(
        arg_x,
        arg_x_scale,
        arg_w,
        arg_w_scale,
        arg_w_exp,
        arg_eids,
        arg_cumsum,
        arg_mind,
        arg_out,
        i32_ntok,
    ):
        lds_ptr = fx.SharedAllocator().allocate(SharedStorage).peek().raw.ptr
        tx = fx.Int32(gpu.thread_id("x"))
        bx = fx.Int32(gpu.block_id("x"))
        lane = tx % fx.Int32(64)
        wave = rocdl.readfirstlane(T.i32, tx // fx.Int32(64))
        cumsum0 = _global_i32_at(arg_cumsum, fx.Int32(0))
        total_m_blocks = cumsum0 // fx.Int32(BM)
        bound = total_m_blocks * fx.Int32(NUM_N_BLOCKS)

        # Bijective XCD round-robin over valid tiles; xcd_swizzle>0 also groups
        # xcd_swizzle m-blocks per XCD for L2 locality.
        NXCD = 8
        xq = _udiv(bound, NXCD)
        xr = _umod(bound, NXCD)

        def _xcd(pid):
            xc = _umod(pid, NXCD)
            wgid = xc * xq + fx.min(xc, xr) + _udiv(pid, NXCD)
            ng = fx.Int32(xcd_swizzle * NUM_N_BLOCKS)
            first_m = (wgid // ng) * fx.Int32(xcd_swizzle)
            group_m = fx.min(total_m_blocks - first_m, fx.Int32(xcd_swizzle))
            wig = wgid % ng
            return (first_m + wig % group_m) * fx.Int32(NUM_N_BLOCKS) + wig // group_m

        if bx < bound:
            if const_expr(xcd_swizzle > 0):
                tile = _xcd(bx)
            else:
                tile = bx
            _body(
                lds_ptr,
                arg_x,
                arg_x_scale,
                arg_w,
                arg_w_scale,
                arg_w_exp,
                arg_eids,
                arg_cumsum,
                arg_mind,
                arg_out,
                i32_ntok,
                tile,
                lane,
                wave,
            )

    @flyc.kernel(name=kname, known_block_size=[256, 1, 1])
    def a8w4_gemm1_kernel(
        arg_x: fx.Int64,
        arg_x_scale: fx.Int64,
        arg_w: fx.Int64,
        arg_w_scale: fx.Int64,
        arg_w_exp: fx.Int64,
        arg_eids: fx.Int64,
        arg_cumsum: fx.Int64,
        arg_mind: fx.Int64,
        arg_out: fx.Int64,
        i32_ntok: fx.Int32,
    ):
        _entry(
            arg_x,
            arg_x_scale,
            arg_w,
            arg_w_scale,
            arg_w_exp,
            arg_eids,
            arg_cumsum,
            arg_mind,
            arg_out,
            i32_ntok,
        )

    @flyc.jit
    def launch(
        arg_x: fx.Int64,
        arg_x_scale: fx.Int64,
        arg_w: fx.Int64,

def run_torch(
    x_fp8, x_scale, w1_qt, w1_scale, sorted_ids, sorted_expert_ids, num_valid_ids, tile_m
):
    """fp32 reference in the kernel's sorted output layout.

    Uses the same FP8 A (dequantized with its row scale) and exact mxfp4 W, so the
    only differences are accumulation order and the bf16 output rounding.
    Returns (ref bf16 [sorted_size, inter], mask of rows the kernel writes).
    """
    tokens, model_dim = x_fp8.shape
    E, n_out, _ = w1_qt.shape
    inter_dim = n_out // 2
    sorted_size = sorted_expert_ids.numel() * tile_m
    nv = int(num_valid_ids[0].item())

    ids = sorted_ids[:nv].to(torch.int64)
    token = ids & 0x00FFFFFF
    row_expert = sorted_expert_ids.to(torch.int64).repeat_interleave(tile_m)[:nv]
    valid = token < tokens
    mask = torch.zeros(sorted_size, dtype=torch.bool, device=x_fp8.device)
    mask[:nv] = valid

    a = x_fp8.to(torch.float32) * x_scale.view(-1, 1)
    w_scale = fp4_utils.e8m0_to_f32(w1_scale).view(E, n_out, model_dim // 32, 1)
    ref = torch.zeros((sorted_size, inter_dim), dtype=torch.float32, device=a.device)
    for e in row_expert[valid].unique().tolist():
        rows = torch.nonzero(valid & (row_expert == e)).squeeze(1)
        w = fp4_utils.mxfp4_to_f32(w1_qt[e]).view(n_out, model_dim // 32, 32)
        w = (w * w_scale[e]).view(n_out, model_dim)
        gate, up = (a[token[rows]] @ w.t()).split(inter_dim, dim=-1)
        ref[rows] = F.silu(gate) * up
    return ref.to(dtypes.bf16), mask


def _cos_diff(x, y):
    x, y = x.double(), y.double()
    return float(1 - 2 * (x * y).sum() / (x * x + y * y).sum())

Looking at 15 loop iterations, I'm trying to figure out why buffer_load issue is stalling for roughly 400-500 cycles each, which adds up to about 2458 cycles per iteration. With 12 loads happening per iteration, I suspect this is a VGPR hazard where loads writing into registers conflict with in-flight reads rather than simply the issue queue being full.

I'm now wondering if it's really the TA/TD queue filling up because all waves fire their loads simultaneously right after the barrier, compared to the original kernel's much lower 765 cycles per iteration. Looking more closely at register allocation, it seems the compiler may be reusing the same physical VGPRs (v[0:3]) for both the old W(kt) values and the new load destinations, which means it has to guarantee the old values are fully consumed before the new load can land — and tracing the instruction order, the VALU decode happens before the barrier and loads, so this reuse could be forcing a wait that explains the stall.

Computing effective memory throughput, I get around 2.9TB/s against a 5.3TB/s HBM peak, and the fact that vmcnt is still waiting ~935 cycles per iteration at the loop top suggests the loads aren't finishing even after the whole compute phase — pointing toward the memory system's queues being saturated rather than compute being the bottleneck now.

I'm checking whether the W dwordx4 loads are properly coalesced: with lanes addressing in a pattern of intra-group offset plus klane stride, 64 lanes cover a contiguous 1KB block, which looks correctly coalesced, while the A loads are gathering rows instead. With glc/sc0 caching mode, the 2.9TB/s figure might actually be near the practical ceiling given limited memory-level parallelism — only around 1.7 workgroups per CU in flight, so I'm estimating per-CU in-flight memory traffic per iteration based on the W tile size.

Working through the math, roughly 40KB per workgroup times 1.7 WGs times 304 CUs gives about 20MB in flight, which by Little's Law would suggest ~10TB/s potential at a few microseconds of latency — so this shouldn't be MLP-limited in theory. But since the vmcnt at the top of each iteration isn't clearing, I suspect HBM latency climbs to 3-5µs under saturation, and the buffer_load stalls likely indicate the TA request queue itself is filling up with limited depth.

This looks like straightforward bandwidth saturation rather than an MLP issue — 12 loads across 4 waves and 2 workgroups means ~96 in-flight requests, which is typical for bandwidth-bound kernels at this point. I want to verify the actual achievable peak against the 2.9TB/s figure by testing a simple copy-like read at the same size, and also try sweeping the cache modifier settings (sc0/nt variations) to see if that changes throughput, plus double-check the kernel's wave span and cycle count to make sure the timing numbers line up.

Working through the traffic accounting: with BM=32 and 256 m-blocks, each expert likely gets one m-block since most have under 29 tokens, and with 2 n-blocks each reading half of W, the weight matrix gets read exactly once (268MB plus 16.8MB of scales), while activations contribute roughly 33MB mostly served from L2. That totals around 300MB+ moved in 97us, giving an effective bandwidth near 3.1TB/s — about 75% of MI300X's measured achievable ceiling of 4.0-4.3TB/s from rocm bandwidth benchmarks, so I'm looking at what's causing that remaining gap, possibly tail effects from the grid size of 512.

Now I'm seeing it's load imbalance across the 304 CUs: 208 CUs get 2 workgroups while 96 get only 1, so the single-workgroup CUs sit idle after finishing, dragging down bandwidth utilization during the tail — total runtime essentially tracks the 2-workgroup CUs' duration. I'm considering fixes like shrinking tile size to rebalance work more evenly, but that runs into VGPR occupancy limits capping concurrent workgroups per CU, so I'd need to cut VGPR usage further to allow more workgroups per CU, or explore split-K, or a persistent kernel with work-stealing instead.

I'm also second-guessing whether the CD swizzle matters here, and shifting focus to testing variants of the b_cache_mod kernel with a smaller tile size to see the effect. Separately, I'm digging into why VGPR usage is so high — suspecting the compiler is hoisting loads and scalar decode work above the sched_barrier, since the loop structure promotes values into fresh virtual registers rather than reusing memory, which could be inflating register pressure unnecessarily.

I'm considering whether adjusting waves_per_eu could force the compiler to target a tighter VGPR budget, though that risks spilling.     Includes RNE subnormals for delta in 12..18; delta >= 19 rounds to zero.
    """
    difference = max_code - group_code
    delta = fx.min(difference, 11).to(fx.Uint32) * fx.Uint32(0x08080808)
    lo = (fx.Uint32(0x6C686080) - delta) & fx.Uint32(0xFFFFFF00)
    hi = fx.Uint32(0x7C787470) - delta

        return (

        (16, 0x01000000, 0x03020201),
        (17, 0, 0x02010100),
        (18, 0, 0x01000000),

        hi = (difference == diff).select(fx.Uint32(high), hi)

    hi = (difference >= 19).select(fx.Uint32(0), hi)

    """Eight consecutive FP4 nibbles (one i32) -> v8 FP8-FNUZ MFMA operand."""
    raw = fx.Uint32(raw)
    low, high = lut
    even = _perm_u32(high, low, raw & 0x07070707)  # nibbles 0,2,4,6
    odd = _perm_u32(high, low, (raw >> 4) & 0x07070707)  # nibbles 1,3,5,7
    parts = []
    for mag, sign in (
        (even, (raw & 0x08080808) << 4),
        (odd, raw & fx.Uint32(0x80808080)),
    ):
        # FNUZ has no -0 (0x80 is NaN): clear the sign of zero-magnitude bytes.
        zeros = (~(mag + fx.Uint32(0x7F7F7F7F))) & fx.Uint32(0x80808080)
        parts.append((mag | sign) & ~zeros)
    lo = _perm_u32(parts[1], parts[0], 0x05010400).bitcast(fx.Int32)
    hi = _perm_u32(parts[1], parts[0], 0x07030602).bitcast(fx.Int32)
    return fx.Vector.from_elements([lo, hi], fx.Int32).bitcast(fx.Float8E4M3FNUZ)"}]}

我改了 [op_tests/test_a8w4_gemm1.py](op_tests/test_a8w4_gemm1.py)。token=512 缺省 shape 下，从原 tuned 配置的约 113us 降到约 83–87us（−23~26%），离显存带宽下限（约 74us）还差 10–15%。所有配置的输出都和原 port kernel 逐位一致，pytest 2 个用例通过。

**token=512（4096/256/256/8）**，同一进程交替测，噪声约 ±3%：

| 配置 | 新 kernel | port 同配置 | 对比原 tuned 配置（port 64×128，约 113us） |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64×128，单 slot | 108–110 | 113 | −3~4% |
| 32×128，预取 | 93–94 | 102 | −17% |
| 32×128，预取 + `xcd_swizzle=1` | **83–87** | 94 | **−23~26%** |
| 32×64，单 slot | 85–87 | 89–92 | −23% |

**prefill**：token=16384 时，64×128 为 733us（port 754），128×128 为 684us（port 701），各快 2–3%。

**改了什么**
1. **fp4→fp8 解码精简**：每个 LUT 额外算一张 sign 掩码表（每个非零项对应 0x80），解码时直接带上符号。这样每个 fragment 不再需要单独修正 FNUZ 的 −0，约 16 条 VALU 降到约 12 条。不需要离线处理权重，所有 BM 都受益。
2. **跨迭代预取**（`pipeline` 参数，缺省在 BM≤32 时打开）：
   - A 的 LDS 改成双缓冲，每个 tile 只留一个 barrier。
   - 计算第 kt 个 tile 前，先发出第 kt+1 个 tile 的 A 和 W 加载；A 先发，这样写 LDS 前只需等 A。
   - 加了 `rocdl.sched_barrier(0)`，否则编译器会把这些预取 load 挪到循环末尾。
3. **A 改为按需从 LDS 读取**，不再一次性把整块 A 读进寄存器，减少寄存器占用。
4. **W 和 scale 的地址在 K 方向上只计算一次**，每个 tile 只加一个统一偏移；同一个 scale dword 只读一次。scale 字节的偏移在编译期就确定，前提是 TILE_K 必须是 256 的倍数（已加断言）。
5. **测试改动**：
   - 计时前先调用一次，把 JIT 编译排除在计时之外。原来首次计时偏慢 10–20%，干扰了对比。
   - 新增与 port 的逐位一致性断言。
   - pytest 同时覆盖 BM=32（预取）和 BM=64（单 slot）。
   - 缺省 tile 改为 32×128 加 64×128，`xcd_swizzle` 缺省改为 1。

**和之前估计不一致的地方**
- 预取只带来约 3% 收益，不是之前估计的 20–30%。改完后 kernel 已经卡在显存带宽上（约 3–3.5 TB/s，上限约 4 TB/s）：load 发射本身就在排队，提前一个 tile 发出的数据到下一轮仍未全部返回。
- 预取让寄存器涨到 230–260 个，在 BM≥64 的 prefill 场景反而变慢（BM=128 时 787us，port 703us）。所以缺省只在 BM≤32 时开启。

**没做的两项及原因**
- **跳过全 padding 的 16 行子块**：BM=32 时 MFMA 只占不到 4% 的时间，收益太小，暂缓。
- **在注册表里加 tile_m=32**：stage1 和 stage2 共用同一个 block_m，而 stage2 的 fp8r 目前只注册了 64/128。需要先验证 stage2 能跑 BM=32，再重新 tune CSV，范围超出这个文件，没有动生产代码。

剩下约 10–15% 的空间主要在两处：WG 之间负载不均（wave 耗时 123k–169k cycle），以及每次迭代只预取一个 tile、在途数据不够。要往下走，得先把预取路径的寄存器降到 168 以内，才能每个 SIMD 跑 3 个 wave，或者预取两个 tile。

children.text: # Compile-time unrolled loop (emitted inline in IR)
Use Python/DSL operators for runtime SSA comparisons. The AST rewriter lowers dynamic `if` conditions to `scf.IfOp`, and comparison operators like `==`, `<`, `>=` generate the needed MLIR predicates.
Use `const_expr(...)` only for values known at trace/compile time, such as Python booleans, constexpr arguments, loop-unroll choices, or type/layout branches:

Do **not** wrap GPU runtime values in `const_expr`. Even with `@flyc.kernel(known_block_size=(256, 1, 1))`, `gpu.thread_id("x")`, `lane`, and `warp_id` are runtime SSA values; the compiler knows their range, not the current lane instance.
When writing or reviewing `@flyc.kernel` / `@flyc.jit` code, proactively avoid these patterns because they can conflict with MLIR construction even if they look valid in plain Python.
1. **Do not define values inside `if/else` and use them later outside the branch.** Keep a single explicit definition path.
2. **Do not mutate captured outer variables inside nested helper functions.** Read-only closure capture is acceptable, but writes should go through explicit parameters and return values.
3. **Avoid early `return`, and do not place `return` / `yield` inside `if/else` branches.** Prefer a single explicit exit so the frontend can determine result types.

4. **Compile-time conditions must use `const_expr(...)`.** Use `if const_expr(flag): ...` for constexpr flags and other static decisions. A plain Python `if` is only safe when the condition is already a Python `bool`.

5. **Runtime branches inside helper functions should be dispatched via local `@flyc.jit`.** When a branch body has side effects, loop-carried values, or branch-local definitions, split the branch bodies into local helpers and wrap the `if` in a local JIT helper:
### Runtime Loops with Loop-Carried Values (Software Pipelining)

Use `init=` on `range()` to create a runtime loop with explicit SSA phi nodes for loop-carried state. This is required for software pipelining (prefetch patterns) where data must flow across iterations.
# Use typed DSL integer bounds (fx.Int64) so the AST rewriter does not treat this as a Python unrolled range.
for iv, state in range(_start, _stop, _step, init=init_state):
results = yield [acc_in] + next_tile  # carry to next iter
# Epilogue: process last tile from results

| `state` | The loop-carried block arguments (phi nodes) for THIS iteration |
| `yield [...]` | Feeds values back as next iteration's `state` |
| `results` | After loop exits, holds the last yielded values |

1. **Loop bounds must be a typed DSL integer such as `fx.Int64(...)`, NOT a plain Python int.** A plain int makes the AST rewriter unroll the loop and silently ignore `init=`. If you write `range(0, 15, 1, init=...)`, the AST rewriter treats the constant bounds as a Python `range` and unrolls; only plain Python-int bounds are unrolled, so a typed bound still produces a runtime `scf.for`. pytest 和缺省 sweep 都加上了 hot experts 用例，pytest 4 个用例全部通过，新 kernel 与 port 的输出逐位一致。

**怎么造不均衡**
- 新增
参数，可选 `"uniform"`（原来的随机路由）或

时随机挑 E/32 个专家（256 个专家里挑 8 个），给它们的 router score 加 2.0，这样大部分 token 的 top-k 都会选中它们。
- 调整强度用两个常量：
（热点专家数量 = E/该值）和

（加多少分）。

**接入方式**
- **pytest**：
的两个取值和

的 32、64 交叉，共 4 个用例。
- **脚本**：新增

，缺省两种都跑。
- **结果表**：新增

、`max tok/expert`、`m-blocks` 三列，方便看分布有多偏。

**缺省运行结果**（token=512）

| routing | tile_m | 每专家最多 token | m-blocks | 新 kernel us | port us |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| uniform | 32 | 29 | 256 | 83.9 | 95.0 |
| uniform | 64 | 29 | 256 | 109.3 | 111.1 |
| hot | 32 | 251 | 312 | 104.5 | 111.7 |
| hot | 64 | 251 | 280 | 108.5 | 112.6 |

有热点专家时，tile_m=32 的优势基本没了（104.5us，接近 tile_m=64 的 108.5us）。原因是热点专家被拆成多个 m-block（251 个 token / 32 ≈ 8 块），同一份权重要重复读多次；tile_m=64 拆得少，重复读也少。

所以 tile_m 不能只按 token 数选，还要看路由有多偏。热点专家能不能在多个 m-block 之间共享读进来的权重（比如让同一专家的 m-block 落在同一个 XCD 上提高 L2 命中，或者一个 WG 处理多个 m-block），可以作为下一步的优化方向。

I'm thinking about using block size 64 but dynamically checking whether the second half of each block (rows 32-63) actually contains valid tokens or just padding. If row 32 is padding, the workgroup can skip to a cheaper 32-row path instead of processing the full 64-row tile, saving work when blocks are only half full.

The performance gain mainly comes from halving MFMA compute and A-tile loads rather than weight reads, since weights are loaded once regardless. Implementing both a 32-row and 64-row path in the same kernel means VGPR allocation gets sized for the worst case between them, which could reduce occupancy slightly, but for small token counts this still fits within acceptable wave limits.

With sorting at BM64 and dynamic skip, hot experts (many tokens) use the full 64-row path to minimize weight re-reads, while cold experts (few tokens) fall back to the 32-row path — giving the best of both. I'm now restructuring the kernel body so the M-dependent logic is parametrized by row count, reusing the same LDS layout for both paths while halving the A-load count for the 32-row case.

Working out accumulator and epilogue handling...

Runtime dispatch logic...

The acc and weight register tensors are defined outside the if, mutated in both branches, so that's fine. For pipelining, I'm weighing using a pipelined BM32-style approach for the half path and a non-pipelined BM64 approach for the full path, since that matches known best performance per size — but mixing means LDS usage becomes the max of both (16KB either way), so I'll parametrize slot size by variant based on row count times tile-K.

Max VGPR usage across variants (230 vs 168) forces 2 waves per SIMD, dropping full-path occupancy from 3 to 2 waves, which could hurt prefill performance for BM64 — though the dynamic kernel mainly targets small/medium token counts. I'm considering making pipelining configurable per variant (default on for half, off for full) tied to a row-count threshold like rows <= 32.

Given the complexity of the current body logic branching on BM, I'm planning to restructure into a `run_tile(m_rows)` helper to unify the logic.

I'm separating the shared weight setup (w_base, w_regs, exponents) from the row-dependent logic (A addressing, accumulator, compute loop, epilogue), with the row-dependent helper called once for static mode or twice for dynamic mode inside a branch, keeping all its values branch-local. I'm double-checking that the sorted_ids indexing for the second half-block (bx_m + BM//2) stays safely within bounds since cumsum0 is a multiple of the block size.

I'm wondering if dyn_m should instead co-compile a half variant without pipelining to cap VGPR at 168, even though that sacrifices the ~3% pipeline benefit on the half path. Worth testing dyn_m with pipeline=False for both variants to see if VGPR drops accordingly, then benchmarking at 512 and 2048 tokens.

response.value:
I'm comparing benchmark results across token counts and routing strategies, checking where the dynamic sort64 approach beats the static32/64 baselines across multiple runs.

At 2048 tokens, both uniform and hot routing favor static64 over dynamic by a wide margin. This surprises me since dynamic should theoretically match or beat static64's workload. I'm suspecting it comes down to occupancy and register pressure—dynamic kernels may use more VGPRs that limit wavefronts per CU, and at 2048 tokens the grid size could push the dynamic approach into needing two scheduling rounds versus one for static64, explaining the slowdown.

So overall, dynamic wins clearly at small token counts but loses at 2048 and in the hot-routing 1024 case, suggesting it's best used as one tuned option among several rather than a universal replacement for static tiling.

I'm thinking about how to wire this into the test and CLI setup: adding a correctness pytest case for dyn_m=True at tile_m=64 across both routings, and extending the parameter sweep to include a dyn_m flag alongside tile_m combinations. For the CLI, I want to keep the default sweep manageable rather than doubling it outright, so I'm considering letting tile entries optionally carry a third value to signal dynamic mode instead of adding a whole separate flag.

I'm thinking about using block size 64 but dynamically checking whether the second half of each block (rows 32-63) actually contains valid tokens or just padding. If row 32 is padding, the workgroup can skip to a cheaper 32-row path instead of processing the full 64-row tile, saving work when blocks are only half full.

The performance gain mainly comes from halving MFMA compute and A-tile loads rather than weight reads, since weights are loaded once regardless. Implementing both a 32-row and 64-row path in the same kernel means VGPR allocation gets sized for the worst case between them, which could reduce occupancy slightly, but for small token counts this still fits within acceptable wave limits.

With sorting at BM64 and dynamic skip, hot experts (many tokens) use the full 64-row path to minimize weight re-reads, while cold experts (few tokens) fall back to the 32-row path — giving the best of both. I'm now restructuring the kernel body so the M-dependent logic is parametrized by row count, reusing the same LDS layout for both paths while halving the A-load count for the 32-row case.

Working out accumulator and epilogue handling...

Runtime dispatch logic...

For pipelining, I'm weighing using a pipelined BM32-style approach for the half path and a non-pipelined BM64 approach for the full path, since that matches known best performance per size — but mixing means LDS usage becomes the max of both (16KB either way), so I'll parametrize slot size by variant based on row count times tile-K.

Max VGPR usage across variants (230 vs 168) forces 2 waves per SIMD, dropping full-path occupancy from 3 to 2 waves, which could hurt prefill performance for BM64 — though the dynamic kernel mainly targets small/medium token counts. I'm considering making pipelining configurable per variant (default on for half, off for full) tied to a row-count threshold like rows <= 32.

- 32 行和 64 行两种算法都编进同一个 kernel，按上面的判断选一条执行。缺省时 32 行那条用预取，64 行那条不预取。
- 为此把和行数有关的部分（A 的地址与加载、累加器、K 循环、写回）收进了 `run_rows(rows)`；W 相关的部分两条路径共用。
- 测试接入：
  - **pytest**：tile 组合为 (32, 固定)、(64, 固定)、(64, `dyn_m`)，再乘两种路由，共 6 个用例。
  - **脚本**：`--tile` 支持写第三个值，比如 `64,128,1` 表示开启 `dyn_m`，缺省会跑这一项。

**实测**（单位 us；每个配置交替跑 3 轮取最小值，单次测量误差有 ±5%）

| token | 路由 | 固定 tile_m=32 | 固定 tile_m=64 | 按 64 排序 + `dyn_m` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | uniform | 83.1 | 105.5 | **82.1** |
| 512 | hot | 102.7 | 108.5 | **98.7** |
| 1024 | uniform | 117.3 | 112.5 | **106.8** |
| 1024 | hot | **114.1** | 132.5 | 124.4 |
| 2048 | uniform | 175.9 | **150.1** | 169.1 |
| 2048 | hot | 173.8 | **149.9** | 162.8 |

**为什么 token 一多就变慢**
1. **寄存器**：两条路径编进同一个 kernel，寄存器按大的那条分配，约 173–234 个 VGPR，每个 SIMD 只能跑 2 个 wave；固定 tile_m=64 只用 168 个，能跑 3 个。2048 token 时 WG 数量超过 2 个 wave 能同时容纳的数量，要分两轮跑。用 `waves_per_eu=3` 强行压到 168 个 VGPR 会出现溢出，速度也没有回来。
2. **负载不均**：热点专家的块走满 64 行，耗时约是 32 行块的 2 倍。所以 1024 token 加热点专家时，WG 大小统一的固定 tile_m=32 反而更快。

**建议**
- **512 token 左右（含热点专家）、1024 token 均匀路由**：开启 `dyn_m`，比原 tuned 配置（约 110us）快约 10–25%。
- **2048 token 及以上**：继续用固定 tile_m=64，不开 `dyn_m`。
- 落地方式：把 `dyn_m` 作为一个额外配置加进 tuning 候选，让 CSV 按 token 数去选，而不是缺省打开。
- 想让它在大 token 时也不吃亏，需要把这个 kernel 的寄存器压到 168 个以内且不溢出，比如 32 行那条也不用预取，同时进一步缩减寄存器占用。这一步我还没做。

"""Standalone A8W4 MoE stage2 (down-proj GEMM + routed atomic scatter) FlyDSL kernel
for gfx942.

Extracted from the a16w4 port (``moe_2stage_a16wmix/gemm2.py``, ``a_dtype="fp8r"``)
with only the configuration the tuned A8W4 build actually runs
(``flydsl_moe2_afp8r_wfp4_bf16_t{BM}x{TN}x{TK}_atomic[_bnt*][_xcd*][_ftz]``):

  * A  : FP8-FNUZ row-quantized stage1 intermediate ``[sorted_size, inter_dim]``
         (by SORTED position) + f32 per-sorted-row scale
  * W2 : mxfp4 (E2M1 + per-1x32 E8M0) ``[E, model_dim, inter_dim/2]``, standard
         N-major preshuffle
  * per-output-channel max E8M0 exponent derived in-kernel from the W2 scales
  * MFMA(16,16,32,fp8) with fp4 -> fp8 decode through a per-32K-group byte LUT
    (+ a sign-mask LUT, so FNUZ -0 never needs a per-fragment fix-up)
  * K (= inter_dim) loop unrolled, XOR-swizzled A-LDS, 4 waves split TILE_N
  * epilogue: acc * a_scale[row] * 2**(exp-132) * route_weight -> LDS -> packed
    bf16x2 global atomic add into ``[tokens, model_dim]``

Run:
    pytest op_tests/test_a8w4_gemm2.py -q
    python op_tests/test_a8w4_gemm2.py -t 512 -s 4096,256,256,8
"""

import flydsl.expr as fx
import pandas as pd
import pytest

from flydsl.expr.typing import Vector as Vec

from aiter.fused_moe import fused_topk, moe_sorting
from aiter.jit.utils.chip_info import get_gfx
from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels.moe_2stage_a16wmix import flydsl_a16w4_gemm2
from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels.moe_2stage_a16wmix.a8w4 import quantize_rows
from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels.moe_2stage_a16wmix.utils import (
    _buffer_i32_scalar_read,
    _global_i32_at,
    _udiv,
    _umod,
)
from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels.mxfp4_gemm_common import (
    _gep1,
    _global_base_ptr1,
    _global_i32_buffer_tiles,
    _global_i32_buffer_view,
    global_typed_ptr,
    lds_typed_ptr,

)
from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels.tensor_shim import _run_compiled
from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels.tensor_shim import _to_raw as _raw
from aiter.ops.shuffle import shuffle_scale_a16w4, shuffle_weight_a16w4
from aiter.test_common import benchmark, checkAllclose, run_perftest
from aiter.utility import fp4_utils

SUPPORTED_GFX = ["gfx942"]  # FP8-FNUZ MFMA + global bf16x2 atomics
TOL_ERR_RATIO = 0.05
ROUTINGS = ["uniform", "hot"]
# "hot" routing: 1/32 of the experts get this score bias, so they land in most
# tokens' top-k (a few experts own a large share of the routed rows).
HOT_EXPERT_DIV = 32
HOT_EXPERT_BIAS = 2.0


# =============================================================================
# Device helpers: fp4 -> fp8 decode, channel factor, MFMA (same as test_a8w4_gemm1)
# =============================================================================
#
# W stays E2M1/E8M0. Output channel n is normalized by 2**(max_exp[n]-127-5)
# (``_channel_factor``, applied in the epilogue); per 32-K group the remaining
# 2**(5-delta), delta = max_exp - group_exp, is folded into an 8-entry
# E2M1-magnitude -> FP8-FNUZ byte table (``_fp8_lut``) so each nibble decodes with
# one v_perm.


def _perm_u32(hi, lo, sel):
    return fx.Uint32(
        rocdl.perm_b32(
            fx.Uint32(hi).ir_value(), fx.Uint32(lo).ir_value(), fx.Uint32(sel).ir_value()
        )
    )


def _fp8_lut(group_code, max_code, flush_tiny):
    """8-entry ``|E2M1| * 2**(5-delta)`` -> FP8-FNUZ byte table.

    Returns ``(lo, hi, sign_lo, sign_hi)``: the magnitude table plus a same-shaped
    mask holding 0x80 for every non-zero entry (FNUZ has no -0; 0x80 is NaN).
    """
    difference = max_code - group_code
    delta = fx.min(difference, 11).to(fx.Uint32) * fx.Uint32(0x08080808)
    lo = (fx.Uint32(0x6C686080) - delta) & fx.Uint32(0xFFFFFF00)
    hi = fx.Uint32(0x7C787470) - delta
    if const_expr(flush_tiny):
        # Approximation: drop groups < 2**-11 of this channel's largest scale.
        lo = (difference > 11).select(fx.Uint32(0), lo)
        hi = (difference > 11).select(fx.Uint32(0), hi)
    else:
        for diff, low, high in (
            (12, 0x0C080400, 0x1C181410),
            (13, 0x06040200, 0x14100C08),
            (14, 0x03020100, 0x0C080604),
            (15, 0x02010000, 0x06040302),
            (16, 0x01000000, 0x03020201),
            (17, 0, 0x02010100),
            (18, 0, 0x01000000),
        ):
            lo = (difference == diff).select(fx.Uint32(low), lo)
            hi = (difference == diff).select(fx.Uint32(high), hi)
        lo = (difference >= 19).select(fx.Uint32(0), lo)
        hi = (difference >= 19).select(fx.Uint32(0), hi)
    # Entries are <= 0x7C, so +0x7F sets bit 7 exactly for non-zero bytes (no carry).
    sign_lo = (lo + fx.Uint32(0x7F7F7F7F)) & fx.Uint32(0x80808080)
    sign_hi = (hi + fx.Uint32(0x7F7F7F7F)) & fx.Uint32(0x80808080)
    return lo, hi, sign_lo, sign_hi


def _fp4x8_to_fp8x8(raw, lut):
    """Eight consecutive FP4 nibbles (one i32) -> v8 FP8-FNUZ MFMA operand."""
    raw = fx.Uint32(raw)
    lo, hi, sign_lo, sign_hi = lut
    sel_even = raw & 0x07070707  # magnitudes of nibbles 0,2,4,6
    sel_odd = (raw >> 4) & 0x07070707  # magnitudes of nibbles 1,3,5,7
    # byte = |value| | (nibble sign & 0x80-if-non-zero)
    even = (_perm_u32(sign_hi, sign_lo, sel_even) & (raw << 4)) | _perm_u32(
        hi, lo, sel_even
    )
    odd = (_perm_u32(sign_hi, sign_lo, sel_odd) & raw) | _perm_u32(hi, lo, sel_odd)
    lo32 = _perm_u32(odd, even, 0x05010400).bitcast(fx.Int32)
    hi32 = _perm_u32(odd, even, 0x07030602).bitcast(fx.Int32)
    return fx.Vector.from_elements([lo32, hi32], fx.Int32).bitcast(fx.Float8E4M3FNUZ)


def _channel_factor(exponent):
    """2**(exponent-127-5) as f32 (subnormal-safe)."""
    normal = ((exponent - 5).to(fx.Uint32) << 23).bitcast(fx.Float32)
    subnormal = (fx.Uint32(1) << (exponent + 17).to(fx.Uint32)).bitcast(fx.Float32)
    return (exponent >= 6).select(normal, subnormal)


def _fp8_frag8(v8):
    t = fx.make_rmem_tensor(fx.make_layout(8, 1), fx.Float8E4M3FNUZ)
    t.store(v8)
    return t

    fx.gemm(mma_atom, acc, _fp8_frag8(a8), _fp8_frag8(b8), acc)

# Epilogue: routing-weighted bf16x2 global atomic scatter (gfx942)
# =============================================================================
